items.snippet: Logistics and transportation companies handle large volumes of invoices for fuel, freight, tolls, and vendor services. Manually recording these expenses can slow down financial tracking and increase the chances of data entry errors. An Invoice OCR API helps automate this process by extracting important information directly from invoice images or PDFs. Using OCR technology, the system can capture details such as invoice numbers, vendor names, dates, line items, and total amounts. This structured data allows businesses to monitor logistics expenses more efficiently, simplify reconciliation, and improve overall financial visibility across transportation operations.

items.title: Invoice OCR API for Automated GST Data Extraction in India
items.snippet: Invoice processing and GST data management can be time-consuming when handled manually. An Invoice OCR API helps automate this process by extracting important information directly from invoice images or PDFs. Using AI-powered OCR technology, the system can detect fields such as invoice number, vendor details, invoice date, line items, and total amounts. It can also capture GST-specific data like GSTIN numbers, HSN/SAC codes, taxable values, and tax amounts. Automating invoice data extraction helps businesses reduce manual entry errors, speed up reconciliation, and simplify GST compliance when handling large volumes of invoices. https://azapi.ai/blog/invoice-ocr-api-with-gst-extraction-india/

items.title: Tell HN: AI coding is sexy, but accounting is the real low-hanging target
items.snippet: Working on automating small business finance (bookkeeping, reconciliation, basic reporting). One thing I keep noticing: compared to programming, accounting often looks like the more automatable problem: It’s rule-based Double entry, charts of accounts, tax rules, materiality thresholds. For most day-to-day transactions you’re not inventing new logic, you’re applying existing rules. It’s verifiable The books either balance or they don’t. Ledgers either reconcile or they don’t. There’s almost always a “ground truth” to compare against (bank feeds, statements, prior periods). It’s boring and repetitive Same vendors, same categories, same patterns every month. items.title: Implementar plot_anomalias() — gráfica de puntos normales vs anómalos
items.snippet: ## Objetivo Crear la función que dibuja las Figuras 4, 5 y 6 del paper: Z contra el tiempo, con **×** para puntos normales y **+** para anómalos. La misma función sirve para cualquier método de detección. ## Archivos - `utils/plots.R`: agregar `plot_anomalias()` **al final del archivo, sin modificar `plot_original_vs_deseason()`**. - `utils/dates.R` (archivo nuevo): función auxiliar `crear_fecha()`. ## Firmas ```r crear_fecha(anio, mes) # Regresa un vector Date con el día 1 de cada mes. # Ej: as.Date(paste(anio, mes, 1, sep = "-")) plot_anomalias(df, anomalo, subtitulo = NULL, paso_y = 1, marcas_x = <ver abajo>) ``` | Parámetro | Tipo | Descripción | |---|---|---| | `df` | data frame | Debe

competitor_references.title: Elaynne/ASR-Game
competitor_references.snippet: This is a template to build games with online speech recognition for brazilian portuguese. This project is responsable for the client side request and can recognize the ordinal numbers from 0 to 9. The custom server side with CNN-BLSTM will be available soon and my research team will teach how to build (all parameters to collect and train) your own grammar.
